pt-en.Às sete da manhã, Alfama ainda pertence: At seven in the morning, Alfama still belongs to the people who live there. The narrow streets smell of coffee and warm bread, and the only sound is a door opening or one neighbor greeting another from window to window.
pt-en.É o bairro mais antigo de Lisboa, e nota: It is the oldest neighborhood in Lisbon, and it shows. The houses lean on one another as if looking for support, and the little stairways climb and fall without asking anyone's leave. Whoever arrives with a map soon finds the map is of little use.
pt-en.O terramoto de 1755 destruiu grande part: The earthquake of 1755 destroyed much of the city, but Alfama, set on firm rock, held up better than the Baixa. That is why its streets still follow the layout of many centuries ago: crooked, tight and full of surprises.
pt-en.Comece no Largo das Portas do Sol, quand: Start at Largo das Portas do Sol, while the sun is still low over the river. From there you can see the rooftops running down to the Tagus, the church towers and, on a clear day, the far bank.
pt-en.Desça depois pela Rua de São Miguel sem: Then walk down Rua de São Miguel, taking your time. The shops are still closed, but the open windows give glimpses of kitchens, cages with little birds and laundry hung out to dry in the wind.
pt-en.Se tiver fome, procure uma pastelaria pe: If you are hungry, look for a small pastry shop, the kind that never appears in the guides. Order a galão and some toast and sit at the counter: that is where you hear the neighborhood's news before it reaches the papers.
pt-en.À noite, Alfama muda de voz. As casas de: At night, Alfama changes its voice. The fado houses turn on their lights, and from half-open doors comes a Portuguese guitar that seems to cry and smile at the same time.
pt-en.Não é preciso perceber a letra para sent: You don't need to understand the words to feel what is sung. Fado speaks of longing, of those who left and those who stayed, and the silence in the room during each song says as much as the music itself.
pt-en.Em junho, o bairro enche-se de manjerico: In June, the neighborhood fills with pots of basil, little paper flags and the smoke of grilled sardines. The Festivals of Saint Anthony turn every square into a street party, and the night of the 12th to the 13th doesn't end before dawn.
pt-en.Se vier nessa altura, reserve com antece: If you come at that time, book ahead and bring comfortable shoes. The cobbled pavements are beautiful but slippery, and the climbs show no mercy to anyone who has already danced all night.
pt-en.Volte ao miradouro de Santa Luzia ao fim: Go back to the Santa Luzia viewpoint at the end of the afternoon. The tiles on the wall tell the city's story, and the golden light on the river makes you forget how tired the stairs left you.
pt-en.Alfama não se visita: vive-se devagar, u: Alfama isn't something you visit: you live it slowly, one street at a time. Whoever walks it calmly takes away more than photographs; they take the rhythm of a neighborhood that never learned to hurry.
